correctness.rationale: All 4096 induced vertex subsets and all twelve cutoffs are exhaustively enumerated from a specified 24-edge graph. Complete finite Hasse-graph topological sorting verifies both augmented and ordinary acyclic Morse matchings with 167180 total incidences. The checker builds five exact integral Morse boundary matrices, verifies their unit minors and the only nontrivial d^2=0 identity. Forman reduction plus Hurewicz classification of consecutive-dimension attaching maps establishes each stated homotopy type; at r=3 a primitive four-cell attachment kills one of two three-spheres. Independent raw simplicial F_2 column reduction checks all persistent intervals, not inferred from stage ranks. Finite exhaustiveness is confined to this graph; output and limitations specify no infinite-family conclusion.

originality.rationale: The previously published same-graph ordinary independence S^2 result is expressly excluded from the novelty contribution. The substantive new statement is the nontrivial cutoff-2-through-7 integral homotopy classification plus full mod-two inclusion barcode; cutoff 1 is known and cutoffs 8 through 12 are classical skeleton endpoints, all included to make the filtration complete. The inspected primary higher-independence sources cover different graph classes or qualitative shellability, not this complete quantitative classification. Two exact same-graph published published-finding corpus RESULT texts were read and do not determine higher cutoffs or inclusion maps. Equivalent unindexed or implicit results remain a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent unindexed or unpublished cutoff classification or barcode might exist; mathematical search non-detection is not a uniqueness proof.
A more general result might imply this exact finite table by specialized calculation not evident in the inspected texts.

Cutoffs 8 through 12 also have classical simplex-skeleton descriptions from four-vertex-connectivity, cutoffs 10 and 11 have general qualitative chordality coverage from Ghosh–Selvaraja, and the initial cutoff-one sphere is previously known; none is an isolated novelty claim.
No independent external mathematical audit or validation has been performed.

value.rationale: The canonical smallest triangle-free 4-regular 4-chromatic graph is a naturally motivated test for higher independence complexes, which are linked to clustered graph coloring. The full integer-cutoff classification and genuine mod-two inclusion barcode are natural invariants, not arbitrary numerical slices. At the intermediate, nontrivial cutoffs, a long-lived three-dimensional class over cutoffs 2 through 4 coexists with a new 63-class burst at cutoff 4; this structural fact is not determined by the known ordinary sphere S^2. The theorem identifies exact integral homotopy types rather than just f-vectors or numerical Betti ranks. Significance is limited to the full finite canonical graph; no general graph-family theorem or integral persistence maps are asserted.
